problem: Navigation foundation models pretrained only on offline videos (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, CityWalker) lack causal or interactive understanding, so they collide with obstacles and pedestrians. RL from scratch in narrow simulators generalizes poorly, and naive full-parameter RL fine-tuning forgets pretrained skills and suffers sim-to-real domain shift.
motivation: Urban robot navigation needs reactive, safe behavior around static obstacles and moving people. Offline data gives perceptual priors but only correlations, and scaling BC data saturates quickly (250k to 750k samples gives only about +2% SR). The paper argues models must move from seeing to experiencing, using RL in simulation on top of video pretraining.
key_idea: Pretrain a multimodal anchor-guided GMM waypoint policy on 100h of navigation video, then RL-finetune only zero-initialized residual copies of the cross-attention layers (RAM) in simulation, keeping the pretrained knowledge intact.
insight: RL post-training gains what scaling offline data cannot: +15% SR on obstacles with no extra offline data, while SFT on rollouts overfits as training cost grows. Where RL is applied matters: fine-tuning the action decoder (DecFT-RL) gives 0.39 SR with gradient explosion, plain SFT gives 0.49, and RAM gives 0.57. The anchor-GMM head is better than discrete or single-mode heads, and comparable to diffusion while being easier to fine-tune with RL.
method: Anchor-Guided Distribution Matching (AGDM): K-Means anchors (M intention points) act as decoder queries; a GMM over waypoints has per-anchor mean/std/correlation, a score, and a velocity scale. Trained with NLL on the mode whose anchor best matches the GT, plus L2 loss on the scale, with dense supervision after each decoder block.

Architecture: DINOv3 encoder over the past 10 frames at 5Hz plus the current frame (10+64 tokens), a goal-point MLP or goal-image tokens, and a 6-layer encoder plus 6-layer decoder (768-d, 8 heads). Goal signals are stochastically masked during training. Outputs are 10 waypoints, robot-agnostic.

Residual-Attention Module (RAM): freeze the pretrained cross-attention and add a trainable parallel copy gated by zero-initialized linear layers. Only the RAM branches are updated during RL, which avoids forgetting and vision-encoder domain shift and is lightweight.

RL fine-tuning: PPO with an entropy bonus using a GMM entropy approximation. The std head is reinitialized to sigma=1 for exploration. A differentiable controller converts waypoints to velocity commands for wheeled, quadruped and humanoid robots. 64 parallel envs in URBAN-SIM (Isaac Sim) with a redesigned procedural urban layout; about 8h on 1 L40S.

Reward design: global goal (dense tanh shaping, +2000 sparse goal, dense and -200 sparse collision), rule regularization (walkable-area termination -10), and human-likeness (trajectory similarity, heading smoothness).

NavBench-GS: closed-loop benchmark of 26 Vid2Sim 3DGS scenes in 4 settings (empty, obstacle, pedestrian, obstacle+pedestrian), with 3DGS backgrounds composited with simulator obstacles and pedestrians. Metrics are SR (<1m from goal, <3 collisions), RC and CT.

setting.backbone: DINOv3 encoder + 6-layer Transformer encoder/decoder with anchor GMM head (pretrained with BC, then RAM finetuned with PPO)
setting.training_data: About 100h of navigation videos (RECON 25h, SCAND 5h, FrodoBots-2K 65h, X-Mobility 2.5h, URBAN-SIM 2.5h) for pretraining; then PPO in URBAN-SIM procedural environments
setting.observation: monocular RGB history (10 frames at 5Hz) + goal point or goal image
setting.action_space: 10 short-term relative waypoints (predicted trajectory), converted by a PD controller to velocity commands
setting.simulator: URBAN-SIM (Isaac Sim) for training; NavBench-GS (3DGS + URBAN-SIM) for evaluation
setting.privileged: none at test time (goal coordinates via odometry/lidar odometry are given)

numbers.extra: 100h video pretraining + RL in URBAN-SIM; wheeled robot in sim

numbers.eval_set_note: 25 real scenarios x 5 repeats; Empty and Obstacle environments

numbers_note: Values are fractions (0-1) exactly as printed. Baseline numbers are not listed. Bold formatting in the main table is inconsistent with the values (e.g., some bold cells are not best).
results: S2E, with only 100h of video, beats all baselines in SR on all four NavBench-GS settings (0.82/0.57/0.74/0.51). MBRA (700h) ties on Obstacle+Pedestrian at 0.51, and CityWalker (2000h) and CityWalker* (100h) are lower. In the real world it reaches SR 0.51 (wheeled) and 0.55 (quadruped) versus 0.32/0.34 for S2E-BC and 0.28/0.31 for CityWalker.
limitations: Vision-only with no 3D perception, so collisions still occur; depth or occupancy prediction is suggested
Evaluation is local waypoint navigation on a self-built benchmark with small real-world tests; absolute SR under obstacles and pedestrians remains around 0.5
RL depends on hand-designed rewards and an in-house procedural URBAN-SIM layout; the humanoid has a low SR (0.21-0.40)
